            <link>https://www.pbs.org/newshour/show/americans-remember-the-lives-lost-in-the-9-11-attacks-25-years-ago</link>
            <description><![CDATA[Families, survivors, first responders and dignitaries marked the 25th anniversary of the 9/11 attacks with somber and poignant ceremonies.             <title><![CDATA[Hillary Clinton reflects on the losses and lessons of 9/11]]></title>
            <link>https://www.pbs.org/newshour/show/hillary-clinton-reflects-on-the-losses-and-lessons-of-9-11</link>
            <description><![CDATA[Twenty-five years ago, Hillary Clinton was the junior senator for the state of New York. This week, she is reflecting on what's been lost and what she has learned since. In her essay for The Atlantic, "What the Aftermath of 9/11 Taught Me," Clinton looks back at how leaders handled public health, national security and transparency after the attacks. She joined Amna Nawaz to discuss more. ]]></description>

            <title><![CDATA[9/11 changed Afghanistan, but now it's back where it started]]></title>
            <link>https://www.pbs.org/newshour/show/9-11-changed-afghanistan-but-now-its-back-where-it-started</link>
            <description><![CDATA[Already scarred by decades of war, Afghanistan became the center of America's response to 9/11 after the Taliban harbored the men who planned the attacks. Over 20 years of what's known there as "The American War," hundreds of thousands, mostly civilians, died. Special correspondent Leila Molana-Allen and videographer Eric O'Connor spoke with three men who fought in that war.]]></description>
            <pubDate>Fri, 11 Sep 2026 18:30:57 -0400</pubDate>
            <guid isPermaLink="true">https://www.pbs.org/newshour/show/9-11-changed-afghanistan-but-now-its-back-where-it-started</guid>
